narrative:
**Week of 2026-10-26 — Hugging Face developer activity**

The headline move was a sharp divergence between model- and Space-side engagement. Model likes fell 24.9% week over week to 8,409 (from roughly 11,200), and are now down 9.4% against the four-week average, while model downloads slipped 8.0% to 3.29M across the 24,638 tracked models — still 1.5% above the four-week baseline, so the weekly drop looks more like normalization than a trend break. Space likes moved the other way, rising 35.1% to 1,375 (from about 1,018) on a base of 7,098 Spaces, and are up 15.6% on four weeks. Family-level model counts were broadly softer: Qwen fell 17.5% to 4,570, Gemma 25.0% to 572, Llama 11.5% to 937, and DeepSeek 50.2% to 213 (though DeepSeek remains 77.9% above its four-week level). GLM/Zhipu (135, +37.8%) and NVIDIA Nemotron (199, +11.2%) were the only meaningful gainers; Mistral held steady at 130. Kimi/Moonshot fell to 29 models from roughly 56 — a thin base where week-to-week swings should not be over-read.

Within Spaces, document-AI was the standout, up 22.1% to 541 Spaces (7.62% share), alongside chat-assistant at 1,120 (+10.0%, 15.78% share) and image-generation at 735 (+6.4%). Scientific-tools reversed hard, down 33.9% to 228 Spaces, with video-generation down 11.7% to 339 and data-analysis down 9.3% to 514. On the technology axis, local-inference (2.70% of Spaces, +12.9%), quantized (2.52%, +11.7%) and diffusion (5.04%, +9.7%) gained, while multimodal (5.33%, -8.5%), vision-language (6.23%, -6.9%) and tool-use (3.10%, -6.7%) eased; long-context rose 65.5% but sits at just 0.39% of Spaces (~28 Spaces), so the percentage is driven by a very small count. By vertical, consumer (10.75%, +17.3%), cybersecurity (2.48%, +18.7%) and e-commerce/retail (4.14%, +11.1%) advanced, against declines in industrial-manufacturing (-18.2%) and scientific-research (-15.1%). SDK mix shifted modestly toward Docker (700, +13.1%) while static (4,064, -3.4%) and Gradio (2,186, -0.2%) were flat to slightly down.

On family share by use case, Qwen extended its lead in coding to 45.0% of 131 classified items (+15.9% w/w), while in chat-assistant (659 items) Qwen slipped to 25.2% (-9.7%) as proprietary-API share rose to 12.4% (+26.0%) and DeepSeek to 5.3% (+45.9%). Two methodology caveats matter here: 12,368 of 24,638 models (50.2%) carry an unknown family label, up 4.5% this week, so family-share readings are based on the classified half only; and several use-case cuts rest on very small denominators — robotics (12), music-generation (31), education (44), "other" (44) and 3D/gaming (40) — where swings such as robotics-Qwen (+400%) reflect a handful of items rather than real adoption shifts. Spaces use-case coverage was complete (1.0) this week; no cells were suppressed. Next week, watch whether model likes rebound toward the four-week average or confirm a genuine downshift, and whether the document-AI and Docker gains in Spaces hold for a second consecutive week.
